title: How Much Do TikTok Ads Cost? Guide for Brands | Pattern
summary: What TikTok ads cost: TikTok's minimum budgets, recommended starting budgets, how bidding works, and the full cost of a TikTok Shop sale, including fees and creator commission.
body_markdown:
TikTok ads have no fixed price. You set a budget and a bid, and TikTok's ad auction decides what each impression, click or sale costs. TikTok requires a daily budget of more than $50 per campaign and more than $20 per ad group. For a purchase campaign with no cost history, TikTok recommends starting at $200 a day. If you sell through TikTok Shop, a sale also carries a referral fee and, for many orders, a creator's commission on top of your ad spend.


This guide covers how TikTok charges for ads, the budgets TikTok sets and recommends, what third-party benchmarks show, and what a TikTok Shop sale really costs once every fee is counted.


## How TikTok charges for ads


Every TikTok ad goes through an auction. Two settings decide what you spend, according to TikTok's[advertising FAQ](https://ads.tiktok.com/business/en-US) :


- Your budget **.** This is the most you'll spend, set per day or for the life of a campaign.
- Your bid strategy **.** TikTok offers two. Lowest Cost gets as many results as possible from your budget. Cost Cap aims to keep the average cost of each result near a figure you choose.


Because it's an auction, the same ad can cost more in one week than the next. Competition for your audience, the quality of your creative and how well your ad matches the people who see it all move the price.


## TikTok's minimum budgets


TikTok sets these minimums:


- Daily budget **:** more than $50 per campaign, and more than $20 per ad group.
- Lifetime budget **:** more than $50 per campaign. For an ad group, the minimum is the number of days it runs multiplied by the $20 daily minimum. A 31-day ad group needs at least $620.


There's no separate minimum spend for a whole campaign beyond these. You may see a "$500 minimum" quoted online, but it isn't in TikTok's current rules.


A few other budget rules are worth knowing before you launch:


- Once a campaign is live, you can change the amount but not switch between daily and lifetime budgets.
- Your campaign budget shouldn't be lower than your ad group budget.
- When an ad group reaches its budget, delivery pauses until the next day or the next budget period.


## How much to budget for TikTok ads


The minimum lets you launch. It usually isn't enough to learn what works. TikTok's[budget best practices](https://ads.tiktok.com/resources/help/article/budget-best-practices) recommend a starting budget based on your goal and whether you already know your cost per result.


### If you don't have a cost per acquisition (CPA) yet:


- $100 a day for awareness, traffic and shallow conversions such as page views
- $200 a day for app installs and deep conversions such as add to cart or purchase


### If you know your CPA:


- 50 times your CPA for awareness, traffic and shallow conversions
- 20 times your CPA for app installs
- 10 times your CPA for deep conversions such as purchases


So a brand with a $25 CPA on purchases would start at about $250 a day per ad group.


TikTok's home page gives a simpler figure: a recommended daily ad group budget of $30 in North America and EMEA, or $20 in APAC. That works as a floor for testing. For a purchase campaign, the help article's goal-based figures are the better guide.


New advertiser credits. TikTok often offers ad credits to new accounts, which must be used within the first 30 days. The offers change, so check[TikTok for Business](https://ads.tiktok.com/business/en-US) for the current terms.


## What TikTok ads cost: benchmarks and why they vary


TikTok doesn't publish average costs. Every cost-per-click or cost-per-thousand-impressions (CPM) figure you'll find comes from a third party, measured on its own customers in a particular year.


Treat any benchmark as a rough range. Your own costs depend on:


- Your category. Beauty, fashion and supplements compete for the same audiences, which pushes prices up.
- Your objective. Paying for purchases costs more per result than paying for views.
- Your creative. Ads that hold attention get more results from the same budget, so weak creative raises your cost per result.
- The time of year. Costs tend to rise in the run-up to major shopping events, when more brands bid for the same audiences.


## What a TikTok Shop sale really costs


If you sell through TikTok Shop, ad spend is only one cost of a sale. A single order can carry four.


1. **** Ad spend. What you pay TikTok to show the ad that led to the sale.


2. **** The referral fee. TikTok Shop charges a referral fee on every order. According to TikTok's[Seller University](https://seller-us.tiktok.com/university/essay?knowledge_id=5988482086864682&lang=en) the fee is the category rate multiplied by what the customer paid plus any platform discount, minus tax. Shipping the customer pays is included in that base. The rate is 6% for most categories, and 5% for several jewelry categories since October 31, 2024.


3. **** The creator's commission. When a creator's affiliate video drives the sale, the creator earns the commission rate you set, anywhere from 1% to 80%. This applies to ads too. If your ad uses a creator's affiliate post, the order still pays that creator a commission, as TikTok explains in its help article on[affiliate commission rates for TikTok Shop Ads](https://ads.tiktok.com/resources/help/article/about-setting-different-affiliate-commission-rates-for-tiktok-shop-ads?lang=en) . Some invited sellers can set a separate, lower rate for ad-driven orders. TikTok's example is a 10% standard rate and a 5% rate for orders that come through an ad. Most sellers pay their standard rate on both.


4. **** Samples. Creators usually need the product before they'll post. Free samples are a real cost of affiliate content, even though they don't appear on any TikTok invoice.


### A worked example


These numbers are made up to show how the costs stack. They aren't benchmarks.


A brand sells a $40 serum with free shipping. A shopper buys after clicking an ad that uses a creator's affiliate video.


- Ad spend for this order: $8 (an ad return of 5 times spend)
- Referral fee at 6%: $2.40
- Creator commission at 15%: $6.00
- Share of sample costs: $2.00 (100 samples worth $10 each, spread across the 500 orders they helped drive)


That's $18.40, or 46% of the sale price, before product cost, fulfillment and returns. The ad dashboard shows a healthy return of 5 times spend. The real cost of acquiring the order is more than twice the ad spend.


This is why your break-even ad return on TikTok Shop is higher than the same product's break-even on a channel without commissions. Work out fees and commission first, then set your ad targets.


## How budgets work for TikTok Shop ads (GMV Max)


For TikTok Shop, budgets work a little differently. GMV Max is TikTok's automated campaign type for TikTok Shop ads, and since July 2025 it's the only supported one. You choose the products, an ROI target and a daily budget, and TikTok decides which videos to run and who sees them.


TikTok doesn't set a separate GMV Max minimum, and it suggests a daily budget during setup. The setting that matters most is your ROI target, and it should come from your margins after the referral fee and commission, using a calculation like the worked example above.


For setup steps, ROI targets and how to read the results, see our[guide to TikTok GMV Max](https://www.pattern.com/blog/tiktok-gmv-max) . For creative and targeting, see[TikTok Shop ads](https://www.pattern.com/blog/tiktok-shop-ads) .


## Are your TikTok ads adding sales?


Knowing what TikTok bills you answers half the cost question. The rest is what you got for it. Some sales credited to an ad would have happened anyway, from a shopper who already knew the brand or saw a creator's organic post. Counting those as ad results makes ads look cheaper than they are.


TikTok also drives sales it doesn't record. Shoppers often discover a product on TikTok and buy it on Amazon.[Pattern's State of Beauty Report](https://www.pattern.com/reports/us-state-of-beauty) shows how large that can be:


- Tarte earned $46M+ on TikTok Shop over six months. Alongside it, Tarte earned $24M+ on Amazon, with 1,300% growth over the same six months.
- Medicube earned $56M+ on TikTok Shop over six months, alongside $117M+ on Amazon and 160% growth.


These figures show TikTok and Amazon revenue side by side, without measuring how much of the Amazon growth TikTok caused. Still, they're a reminder that a TikTok dashboard can undercount ads' value by missing sales elsewhere, and overcount it by crediting sales that would have happened anyway.


Two questions help:


1. How many of these sales would have happened without the ad? That's incrementality. Holdout tests, where part of the audience doesn't see your ads, are the most direct way to measure it.
2. What happened on your other channels while the ads ran? Watch Amazon branded search and sales for the products you're promoting on TikTok.


## How to keep TikTok ad costs under control


- **Leave new campaigns alone during the learning phase.** TikTok advises against changing targeting, bids or budgets until it ends.
- **Raise budgets in steps.** TikTok's About budgets article says to raise a budget by no more than 40% at a time during the learning phase and 30% after it, and no more often than every two days. Its best practices article gives a looser 50%, so the stricter figures are the safer guide.
- **Start with daily budgets.** TikTok recommends daily over lifetime budgets while you learn.
- **Feed the auction good creative.** Refresh ads before performance fades, and use creator content that looks native to TikTok.
- **Set your targets on full cost.** Base your CPA and ROI targets on ad spend plus referral fee, commission and samples.

## Frequently asked questions


### How much do TikTok ads cost per day?


TikTok requires more than $50 a day per campaign and more than $20 a day per ad group. For a purchase campaign with no cost history, TikTok recommends $200 a day. If you know your cost per purchase, TikTok recommends 10 times that figure each day.


### What is the minimum budget for TikTok ads?


More than $50 per campaign and more than $20 per ad group for daily budgets. For a lifetime ad group budget, the minimum is $20 multiplied by the number of days it runs.


### How much does TikTok Shop take per sale?


TikTok Shop charges a referral fee on each order: 6% for most categories, calculated on what the customer paid plus any platform discount, minus tax, including shipping the customer pays. If a creator's affiliate content drove the sale, the creator's commission is paid on top. Learn more in[how TikTok Shop works](https://www.pattern.com/blog/how-does-tiktok-shop-work) .


### Do TikTok ads that use creator videos still pay commission?


Yes. An order from an ad that uses a creator's affiliate post still earns that creator a commission, at your standard rate unless you're an invited seller with a separate rate for ad-driven orders.


### Do I need an agency for TikTok ads?


Not to start. TikTok Ads Manager is self-serve. Brands selling on TikTok Shop at scale often work with a partner that manages ads, creators and fees together, because those costs interact on every order.
